To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
phosphorylation of NS5A at threonine 242 and 244 is important for efficient replication of HCV and that this phosphorylation is required for the normal intracellular localization of NS5a.
threonine phosphorylated NS5A negatively regulates virus genome replication and that the phosphorylation state of NS5A may influence the intracellular distribution of this protein.
phosphorylation of the non-structural protein NS5A is important for the replication of the hepatitis C virus and that the phosphorylation state of this protein affects the subcellular localization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of phosphorylation sites within the hepatitis C virus nonstructural protein NS5A.
the role of NS5A phosphorylations in regulating the replication cycle of HCV and how this is related to the localization of NS5As.
the role of NS5A phosphorylated residues in the regulation of virus replication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phosphorylation state of NS5A at these sites is important for both virus genome replication as well as virus particle assembly.
phosphorylation of NS5A at the three residues examined here negatively regulates virus RNA synthesis and that phosphorylation of T244 and T242 are more important for this regulation.
NS5A phosphorylated on T242 and/or T244 inhibits viral RNA replication and that the phosphorylation status of NS5A is critical for its intracellular localization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
phosphorylation of T242 and T244 in NS5A is important for the efficient production of infectious virus.
phosphorylation of T242 and T244 negatively regulates the RNA synthesis function of NS5A and that phosphorylation of these sites is important in determining the basally phosphorylation state of NS5A.
phosphorylation of the serine-rich domain of NS5A negatively regulates HCV genome replication and the assembly of infectious virus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the threonine residues in NS5A are phosphorylated and that the modification has a role in virus replication.
NS5A phosphorylated at T242 and T244 is inhibitory to virus genome replication.
phosphorylation of NS5A at specific residues is important for virus genome replication, but that this phosphorylation is not essential for the production of infectious virions.
